instructions: On Sunday, or up to 4 days ahead: Heat the oven to 350°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, mash the 3 bananas with a fork until they're mostly smooth. That should be about 1 1/2 cups.
Stir in the egg, 1/3 cup yogurt and 1 tsp cinnamon. Add the 2 cups oats and the 1/2 cup chocolate chips and stir until everything is coated.
Put the bowl in the fridge for 15 minutes.
Scoop the dough into 12 mounds on the baking sheet, about 1/4 cup each. Press the tops flat with your fingers.
Bake for 20 minutes, until the middles are set. This makes 12 cookies.
Let them cool on the pan for 10 minutes, then lift them onto a rack to cool completely.
They keep in a sealed container on the counter or in the fridge for up to 4 days. For the freezer, transfer them into a freezer bag. They keep for up to 3 months.
In the morning, eat two as they are, or microwave them for about 20 seconds to warm them. From frozen, microwave for 30 to 40 seconds.
advance_prep_notes: Bake the batch on Sunday, or up to 4 days ahead, and keep them in a sealed container.
method_notes: The sources all mash ripe bananas with oats and bake them as soft cookies. Dizzy, Busy and Hungry (the lead, titled Oatmeal Banana Cookies) binds with an egg and vanilla Greek yogurt, chills the dough 15 minutes, and gives the keeping times. Family Fresh Meals uses applesauce and no egg, and Lynn's Kitchen Adventures adds brown sugar, butter and baking powder. No breakfast cookie page had 20 ratings, so the lead is the best-rated real oat and banana cookie. This uses 1/2 cup of chocolate chips where the lead uses 1 cup, to suit breakfast.
